captive_summary: The only sizeable gas-fired plant near the terminal — the GOGPT-flagged 1,140 MW facility — is the Dongya Electric (Yangjiang) High-Tech Zone natural gas cogeneration project (东亚电力(阳江)高新区天然气热电联产项目), owned and operated by East Asia Electric Power (Yangjiang) Co., Ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Pacific Energy Group (太平洋能源集团) — a different company from the terminal owner, Guangdong Yangjiang Hailingwan LNG Co Ltd. It is a commercial cogeneration plant selling steam (~720,000 t/yr) and power (~1 billion kWh/yr) to the industrial park/grid, not an on-site/fenceline plant powering the LNG terminal's own operations. This is the industrial-host trap: a colocated but separately-owned, separately-purposed plant.
confirmed_how: Thepaper.cn (2023-09-26) and the Yangjiang high-tech-zone government portal both name East Asia Electric Power (Yangjiang) Co Ltd — 'a wholly-owned subsidiary of Pacific Energy Group' — as investor/builder/operator of the 2x120 MW Phase 1 units (of a planned 1,140 MW total, matching the GOGPT figure exactly), producing steam and power for commercial sale. The Guangdong provincial tax bureau's article corroborates the same ownership and project description. None of the three sources ties this plant to the LNG terminal's own power supply; the terminal owner (Guangdong Yangjiang Hailingwan LNG Co Ltd) is not mentioned in connection with the power plant.
